note: One narrow idea per Short. Public-domain book; hooks and examples in our own modern words.

episodes.title: The two lists
episodes.hook: Everything in your life fits on one of two lists.
episodes.angle: Things up to you (your choices) and things not up to you (others, results). Peace starts with sorting. Example: a job interview, where your prep is yours and the hiring decision is not.

episodes.title: Why you're anxious
episodes.hook: Anxiety is wanting something you don't control.
episodes.angle: Suffering comes from attaching desire to things outside our power. Example: refreshing your phone for a reply that only they can send.

episodes.title: It's not the thing
episodes.hook: It's not things that upset you. It's what you believe about them.
episodes.angle: Judgments disturb us, not events. Example: a spilled coffee that ruins one person's day and makes another laugh.

episodes.title: Want what happens
episodes.hook: Stop wishing things go your way. Wish they go the way they go.
episodes.angle: Aligning desire with reality removes disappointment. Example: rain on the day of the picnic turned into a board-game afternoon.

episodes.title: 'I lost it' vs 'I gave it back'
episodes.hook: Never say 'I lost it'. Say 'I gave it back'.
episodes.angle: Everything is borrowed, so losing it is returning it. Example: a stolen bike, a broken phone, an ended friendship.

episodes.title: Start with a cracked cup
episodes.hook: Practice on small losses before life gives you big ones.
episodes.angle: Train your calm on small things first. Example: staying calm about a cracked mug as practice for a real setback.

episodes.title: Love it as it is
episodes.hook: If you love a mug, remember it's a mug.
episodes.angle: Remind yourself what things are, so their end doesn't crush you. Example: enjoying your first car while knowing it won't last forever.

episodes.title: Let them think you're a fool
episodes.hook: If you want to grow, be okay with looking stupid.
episodes.angle: Progress requires letting others think you're foolish. Example: the beginner at the gym using the lightest weights while others stare.

episodes.title: Someone insulted you?
episodes.hook: Nobody can insult you without your help.
episodes.angle: An insult only lands if you agree with it. Example: someone calls you bald when you have a full head of hair, and nothing happens.

episodes.title: Say less about yourself
episodes.hook: The more you talk about your wins, the smaller they get.
episodes.angle: Don't boast or lecture; show it through action. Example: the friend who quietly runs every morning versus the one who posts about running.

episodes.title: Don't judge, describe
episodes.hook: He doesn't drink too much. He drinks a lot. That's all you know.
episodes.angle: Judge actions only by facts, not assumptions. Example: a coworker who leaves early may have a sick child.

episodes.title: You didn't pick the role
episodes.hook: You didn't choose your role in life. You choose how well you play it.
episodes.angle: We are actors in a play; the casting isn't ours, the acting is. Example: the extra in a movie who makes three seconds unforgettable.

episodes.title: Life is a banquet
episodes.hook: Treat life like a dinner party. Wait for the plate to reach you.
episodes.angle: Take what comes politely, don't grab what passed or isn't here yet. Example: the friend who waits his turn and still gets the best slice.

episodes.title: Start now, not later
episodes.hook: How long will you wait before you demand the best of yourself?
episodes.angle: You're not a child anymore; stop postponing your progress. Example: the person who 'will start Monday' for two years.

episodes.title: The Olympic athlete
episodes.hook: You want to win the Olympics? Then count the cost first.
episodes.angle: Before starting anything, look at what it truly demands. Example: someone who wants to become a writer but doesn't want rejection letters.
